metadata.note: The Missouri-Kansas-Texas ('Katy') lines in Texas, 1873-1964, with the 1880-1888 Missouri Pacific lease era split out as separate features over identical geometry (Rule 4). One Katy colour for every Katy era: the Missouri, Kansas & Texas Railway (to 1891), its Texas subsidiaries the Missouri, Kansas & Texas Railway of Texas (from 1 Jan 1892) and Missouri-Kansas-Texas Railroad of Texas (reorganized 1 Apr 1923, NOT consolidated then), and the parent MKT from 1 Jul 1960. The Texas company was a wholly controlled subsidiary required by Texas law (directors nominated by the parent, stock in trust for the parent's holders - ICC), the through trains were sold as one 'Katy Lines' system, so it is treated as one operator; if a maintainer reads Rule 4 literally the split dates would be 1 Jan 1892 and 1 Jul 1960 - never 1923. Receivership (1888-91, 1915-23) and USRA control (1918-20) are not split. Lines already drawn elsewhere and not repeated here: Houston - Galveston Katy trackage (galveston_houston_and_henderson_railroad.geojson, katy-houston-galveston) and Wichita Falls - Forgan (wichita_falls_northwestern.geojson). Trackage-rights pieces drawn as Katy features: Whitesboro - Fort Worth (Texas & Pacific) and Austin - San Marcos (I&GN).
sources: Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt)
not_yet_sourced: OPEN END 1964: the Dallas - Waco - Austin - San Antonio and Red River - Denison - Dallas main lines are drawn to 1964, the year every source agrees on. Conflict: Katy RR Historical Society (all passenger service ended 24 May 1964 at Waco), Waco Tribune (last Waco departure 26 Jul 1964), Wikipedia/streamlinerschedules (a Kansas City - Dallas Texas Special remnant ran to 30 Jun/1 Jul 1965). If the 1965 remnant is accepted, Red River - Denison - Dallas could extend to 1965.

OPEN END 1957: Denison - Fort Worth, Fort Worth - Hillsboro and the Wichita Falls line (Whitesboro - Henrietta - Wichita Falls): confirmed in the 28 Apr 1957 timetable, gone by Nov 1959; no source dates the cut.

OPEN END 1951: Greenville - Mineola, San Marcos - Lockhart - Smithville and the Belton Branch are confirmed only by the Feb 1952 Official Guide (tables dated 1950-51). Upper bound only: streamlinerschedules says the two trains of Sep 1960 were 'the last passenger service on the Katy system'.

ANCHORS: Dallas - Denton 1917 (a Carrollton joint-station lease, not a timetable; freight-only by 1951) and Stamford - Rotan 1951 (Official Guide Table 14, 'Motor' read as a rail motor car, not a bus). Each is the only confirmed year.

OPEN BOTH ENDS: McKinney - Waskom 1911-1917 and Trinity - Colmesneil 1909-1917 rest on ICC facility leases (Jefferson, Groveton) with 1917 rents. The Katy tenures (1901-1923 and 1888-1923) are almost certainly the true spans but no timetable confirms them.
All start years are construction years (ICC/TSHA); no first passenger train was verified for any line. The Missouri Pacific lease's exact voiding date in 1888 is not established.
Houston line end: Union Pacific's 'passenger service in Katy ended on November 23, 1957' is a station date applied to the whole Taylor - Houston line.
Boggy Tank (Taylor - Houston construction break 1887-1893) is not located; whether trains ran to the stub end before 1893 is not established.

Not drawn for lack of a confirmed passenger year: Texas Central Waco - Albany - Stamford under the Katy (1914-, freight-only by 1951), De Leon - Cross Plains, Denison (Ray) - Sherman, and the 1914 lessors Wichita Falls & Southern, Beaumont & Great Northern, Denison Bonham & New Orleans. Not drawn as candidate trackage blocks: I&GN San Marcos - San Antonio (c.1893-1901) and pre-1916 Katy running to Galveston.
Not drawn for geometry: Waskom - Shreveport VS&P trackage (1900 alignment not identified - see katy-mckinney-waskom geometry_quality).
